full_judgment: 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that in pursuance of an agreement dated 18.7.2001, the plaintiff-respondent entered into the suit-shop owned by the defendant-respondent as a monthly tenant. But inspite of receipt of advance from the plaintiff, the defendant was trying to let out the suit-shop premises to a third party, as such, the plaintiff filed a suit being Title Suit No. 14 of 2005 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal, praying for inter alia, for a decree that the defendant be restrained by an order of permanent injunction not to let out the shop premises in favour of anybody else during the period of the agreement between them. Besides, an application under Order XXXIX rules 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, praying for an order of temporary injunction on disposal of the suit was filed. The plaintiff also, prayed for an order of ad-interim injunction restraining the defendant from letting out the suit shop premises which is being reconstructed by the City Corporation, to any one else till disposal of the petition for temporary injunction. In response, the defendant filed a written objection to the petition for temporary injunction, denying all material allegations stated therein.
